notes.meaning: A teacher calls on his student to listen closely to what he has learned about life. This advice comes from God's wisdom and long, personal experience. Listening carefully is the first step to staying safe from foolish choices.

Listening to wise guidance helps a person think ahead and make sound choices. It also guards speech, so that words are helpful, true, and guided by God's truth. Speaking what is right helps protect someone against persuasive, harmful words.

The temptation to be unfaithful often arrives through sweet and flattering words. Seduction sounds gentle, pleasant, and harmless at first, like sweet honey or smooth oil. These smooth words hide the deadly trap beneath them.

What begins with sweet promises soon turns to sharp pain and deep regret. The result of sexual sin is like wormwood, an extremely bitter herb, and cuts like a sword with two edges. It wounds a person's conscience, health, and life.

The path of the unfaithful woman leads straight down to physical ruin and the grave. In Scripture, Sheol refers to the place of the dead. Her lifestyle draws those who follow her away from life and toward destruction and God's judgment.

The temptress wanders along unsteady paths without even realizing how dangerous they are. She does not stop to reflect on where her lifestyle leads, so she keeps shifting and making excuses. Because she ignores God's way of life, she drags others into the same aimless wandering.

The teacher pauses to address his listeners directly and urge them not to forget his warning. He knows young people are especially open to being led astray by strong desires. Holding tightly to godly instruction gives the strength needed to stand firm against temptation.

The best way to resist sexual temptation is to stay as far away from it as possible. A person should not test their own willpower by walking near places or situations where trouble waits. True safety comes from running away from danger before it begins.

Giving in to lust robs a person of their youth, dignity, and best years of life. Instead of using strength for good, the sinner wastes it on a partner or lifestyle that shows no true mercy. Those who lead others into sin do not care about their well-being and will gladly ruin them.

Immorality quickly drains a person's hard-earned money and possessions. What should have supported a family and built up a home ends up squandered on strangers. Sin often leaves people financially ruined and empty-handed.

Sin eventually ruins physical health, bringing pain and disease in place of pleasure. Looking back when life is nearly over, the sinner can only groan in deep regret over a wasted body. The short excitement of rebellion leaves behind lasting physical decay.

In the end, the ruined person remembers all the good advice they stubbornly rejected. They bitterly confess that they hated correction and ignored the warnings of parents and teachers who cared for them. Looking back, they realize their own pride and stubbornness caused their downfall.

The sinner faces public disgrace and severe punishment before their own community. In Israel, serious sins could bring someone before the gathering of elders and the public court for judgment. What was done in secret finally brings total shame in the open light.

Solomon presents God's appointed cure for sexual sin, which is the blessing of faithful marriage. A cistern and well represent one's own spouse, who provides pure and refreshing satisfaction. God wants husbands and wives to find full joy and contentment with each other at home.

Intimate love is meant to stay private and treasured, not scattered wastefully in public streets. Solomon asks why anyone would throw away what is holy and precious on casual or illicit relationships. God designed marriage to be protected from the public square.
The intimate bond between husband and wife belongs strictly to them. It must never be shared with outsiders or polluted by infidelity. True marital happiness depends on complete, shared loyalty.

A husband is encouraged to delight in the wife he married in his youth and to ask God's blessing on their union. A peaceful and joyful marriage is one of God's greatest earthly gifts. Cherishing one's spouse guards the heart from wandering desires.

Scripture openly celebrates the romantic and physical joys of marriage using gentle images like a deer or gazelle. God intends physical affection between a husband and wife to bring lasting satisfaction and delight. Being warmly captivated by one's own spouse protects against the lure of outside temptation.

Solomon questions why a man would choose the dangerous embrace of another woman when he can have pure love at home. Adultery is not just wicked, but utterly foolish and unreasonable. Seeking love outside of God's covenant always brings grief instead of peace.

God sees every action, whether done in broad daylight or behind closed doors. He does not merely glance at human behavior; He carefully weighs and examines every step a person takes. Knowing that the Lord watches everything should create a healthy reverence that keeps people from secret sins.

Sin acts like a trap that catches the very person who set it. A sinner might think they can stop their bad behavior at any time, but repeated wrongdoing forms tight cords of habit that become impossible to break alone. The evil a person chooses ends up becoming their prison.

The unrepentant sinner perishes because he refused to accept guidance and self-control. His downfall is not caused by ignorance, but by stubbornly choosing foolishness over God's wisdom. Refusing correction leads directly to ruin and spiritual death.
